correctness.rationale: On curvature-one S^3, Haar t=|z1|^2 is uniform; group powers give exactly two orbit-distance classes, each with five unordered pairs. All triples contain both pair classes, and their maximum is at least acos(-1/4), so no triple cap overlaps occur below half this radius. Spherical tubular coordinates yield I(r,d)=2π[r−d/2−cos²r(tan r−tan(d/2))], valid for d<2r<π. The quotient-ball union and 2π²/5 volume give a one-dimensional exact integral, elementary evaluation gives the stated B_a(r); Taylor expansion gives K=10(√5−1)/(3π). High-precision independent quadrature and directly sampled 2,000,000 Haar pairs corroborate; finite checks are not infinite proof.

value.rationale: L(5,2) is the simplest inhomogeneous order-five spherical lens space and is a named numerical example/analytical target in the closest 2020 distance-distribution paper. The exact first-overlap CDF on a nonzero interval and a sharp cubic cut-locus contact exponent (versus quadratic in homogeneous L(5,1)) provide natural geometrically interpretable distributional information rather than an arbitrary numerical invariant. The restriction to the initial cap-overlap regime is explicit.
